purpose: Proposed direct Tools-runner case bodies for three empty inventory cases. No runtime, role, permission, or inventory result is claimed.

console.control: Visible #consoleLog button invokes helloWorld(), which calls console.log('Hello, world!'). The page also has a separate console-error button. Verify the served page still has this exact button/function before native execution; if it changed, stop as fixture unavailable.

network_and_body.response_oracle: The public GET response contains the literal <title>Web form</title> and form controls. Recheck live bytes/status at execution time; do not treat this dated hash as a permanent server guarantee.

shared_setup.identity: After admitted resource permit, in separate disposable Chrome profiles for member and admin load the exact candidate extension. Record source commit, lockfile hash, build receipt, extension ID/version/Loaded from path, browser version, signed-in role, and target tab ID. In each profile confirm this Chrome build declares debugger as a required manifest permission and independently check chrome.permissions.contains({permissions:['debugger']}) in that profile's extension context before the positive Tools run; admin may also inspect Settings > Advanced agent capabilities > DevTools Protocol installation-granted status. There is no optional debugger switch or request gesture: a false/unavailable status is a build/browser permission precondition failure, not a handler result. Guest cannot reach signed-in Tools; guest denial is a separate Tools UI case.
shared_setup.manual_path: Focus only the disposable public Selenium tab. In Tools > Catalog choose All handlers; search the exact handler name, verify its privileged tier/schema, enter the listed JSON with the owned decimal string tab_id, Run, and read inline output/error. list_open_tabs {} identifies the exact URL and tab ID. No account or credential page may be captured, and do not copy full network headers or unrelated console text into evidence.
shared_setup.warm_reload: Run a warm pass without an immediately preceding full extension Reload. Then Reload that exact extension in chrome://extensions, confirm ID/version/path, reopen Tools, reload the public fixture in an owned tab, reacquire tab ID, rearm capture and repeat. A page reload or side-panel reopen alone is not an extension Reload. Service-worker restart may clear in-memory CDP buffers, so no warm request_id or console count carries into post-reload.
shared_setup.permission_boundary: Tools Run calls handler.run directly with permissionMode=act and assignedTabId=null; it bypasses dispatcher confirmation and does not prove privileged-card denial, request-time role advertisement, or assigned-tab isolation. All three original permissions dimensions remain unresolved. A separate dispatcher case needs a proven exact advertised call for each tested role, a baseline capture state before the call, the tester choosing Deny in the actual privileged approval UI, a structured denial result, and an unchanged owned page/capture state. The current manual route cannot supply that approval card, and source metadata alone does not prove an executable agent-call route; do not claim these separate cases designed or run. Malformed input, missing required debugger permission, and CDP attach failure are not privileged-card denial.
shared_setup.attachment_cleanup: Admin records cdp_attached_tabs and owned debugger banner before and immediately after positive capture, then uses cdp_detach only for the exact new owned tab ID if still attached and verifies disappearance. If already idle/worker-detached, record that state separately. Member must not use admin-only helpers through the manual gate bypass; close only the disposable owned tab and verify its banner clears. Preserve all baseline attachments and unrelated tabs.

proposed_case_patches.name: read_console_messages
proposed_case_patches.source_readiness: Executable direct-manual source procedure conditional on the public page retaining #consoleLog and the exact Hello, world! fixture; actual member/admin, debugger and dispatcher results unverified.

preconditions: In this role/profile, independently verify the candidate Chrome extension includes and currently has its required debugger permission before positive capture; no optional debugger toggle exists. If absent, stop as build/browser precondition failure.

Shared setup above; open only the public Selenium log-entry fixture in a disposable tab. Verify the visible #consoleLog control and its helloWorld console.log('Hello, world!') source before execution.
Record exact owned tab ID; capture must start before clicking #consoleLog. Any prior console buffer or debugger attachment on that tab requires a fresh disposable tab, not an assumed empty buffer.
steps: Warm: in Tools run read_console_messages {"tab_id":"$TAB_ID","auto_start":true,"pattern":"^Hello, world!$","clear":false}. Require {ok:true,count:0,messages:[]} before the page action; this arms Runtime capture. If nonempty, stop and use a fresh disposable tab.

Click the web page's visible #consoleLog button once through ordinary browser UI, without submitting anything. In Tools run the same read_console_messages JSON again; inspect only the matching output fields.

Positive: require exactly one message with level log, text Hello, world!, owned Selenium URL and a timestamp after capture was armed. Re-run with clear:false to confirm peek retains it; then run the same pattern with clear:true to consume it and one final clear:false read that returns count 0. Record the owned attachment/banner immediately after the first positive read.

Empty filter: run {"tab_id":"$TAB_ID","auto_start":false,"pattern":"^absent-4115$","clear":false}; require count 0 without treating it as proof the whole buffer is empty. Schema-negative: {"tab_id":"$TAB_ID","limit":0} must show Schema mismatch and no handler execution.
Repeat all positive/empty/error segments after full extension Reload on a fresh/rearmed tab. Use exact owned attachment cleanup from shared setup.
expected: After the page button, the inline result has ok:true,count:1 and exact log text/level from the public fixture; before the button and after explicit consumption, the exact-match query is empty. Generic page console noise is not an oracle.

clear:false peeks; clear:true removes up to limit before regex filtering, so only use clear:true after isolating this disposable fixture. A regex miss returns zero matching messages, not a buffer-wide absence claim.
limit:0 is local schema rejection, not debugger denial. No unrelated page or console buffer is read or cleared.
This direct Tools procedure does not verify the original permissions dimension; a separate proven dispatcher invocation and privileged-card Deny result are still needed for each role.

proposed_case_patches.name: read_network_requests
proposed_case_patches.source_readiness: Executable direct-manual source procedure conditional on the public Web form GET fixture; actual capture and permission outcomes unverified.

preconditions: In this role/profile, independently verify the candidate Chrome extension includes and currently has its required debugger permission before positive capture; no optional debugger toggle exists. If absent, stop as build/browser precondition failure.
Shared setup above; open the public Selenium Web form in a new disposable tab and confirm current HTTP 200, title marker and visible form before capture. Capture only this unauthenticated tab.
Record exact owned tab ID. A fresh tab or clean capture is needed; read_network_requests drains records on every call even when clear:false. It returns request metadata, not inline response bodies.
steps: Warm: in Tools run read_network_requests {"tab_id":"$TAB_ID","url_pattern":"/selenium/web/web-form.html","auto_start":true,"limit":100}; require count 0 before triggering a new request; this arms Network capture after the initial load. If nonzero, begin with a fresh owned tab.

Reload only that Web form tab once through normal browser UI; wait for the visible Web form. Run the identical read_network_requests JSON promptly; record all matching safe URL/status/method/request_id fields from this disposable tab. A clean pass has exactly one completed final public document GET with status 200, finished:true, failed not true, mime_type text/html and nonempty request_id. If multiple same-URL records or a redirect occur, classify against the observed page/fixture before judging the handler; select only the completed final 200 GET for 4117 and stop if ambiguous. Do not persist headers or unrelated URLs.

Immediately record owned debugger banner/admin attachment delta. Re-run the same filter without another reload; require count 0 because drainNetworkCapture splices the buffer. Use a unique impossible URL substring in a fresh/no-new-request read for the empty filter. Schema-negative: {"tab_id":"$TAB_ID","limit":0} must show Schema mismatch.

Repeat warm and post-extension-Reload phases with a fresh request_id. For 4117, do not detach, close the tab, stop Network capture or reload the extension before get_request_body; then perform exact owned cleanup.
expected: The bounded positive record identifies the actual post-arm public document GET, completion, HTTP 200 and text/html, with request_id usable while the same CDP session lives. A response before capture was armed is not evidence.

A second read with no new navigation returns count 0 because the implementation drains all queued records before URL filtering. include_body and clear inputs are accepted but unused by this handler; do not claim they changed behavior.

limit:0 is schema refusal, not permission denial. A missing, failed or unfinished final document record leaves positive unverified. Extra matching records or redirects require fixture/browser classification and are not by themselves a handler defect.
This direct Tools procedure does not verify the original permissions dimension; a separate proven dispatcher invocation and privileged-card Deny result are still needed for each role.

proposed_case_patches.name: get_request_body
proposed_case_patches.source_readiness: Executable direct-manual response-body procedure only when 4116 has just captured one completed public Web form GET in the same live CDP session; standalone request-body capture is not implemented.

preconditions: In this role/profile, independently verify the candidate Chrome extension includes and currently has its required debugger permission before positive capture; no optional debugger toggle exists. If absent, stop as build/browser precondition failure.

Shared setup above; complete the 4116 arm/reload/read segment on the same disposable public Selenium Web form tab. Keep its exact completed GET request_id, tab ID and live CDP attachment; no extension Reload, tab close, detach or Network.disable between capture and body read.

This handler's name is misleading: it delegates to Network.getResponseBody for a captured request ID. It does not return a POST request payload. Recheck the public page's current HTTP 200 text/html source and literal <title>Web form</title> marker before treating the body as an oracle.
steps: In Tools > Catalog > All handlers open get_request_body and run {"tab_id":"$TAB_ID","request_id":"$CAPTURED_REQUEST_ID"}, replacing both values with the just-observed 4116 result from this tab/session.

Positive: require ok:true, nonempty body and base64_encoded boolean. Decode only if true; require decoded UTF-8 HTML includes the exact <title>Web form</title> marker and visible form-control text from the independently checked public fixture. Do not record the full body or headers in the inventory receipt.

Error: run {"tab_id":"$TAB_ID","request_id":"missing-request-id-4117"}; require ok:false with an explicit CDP reason, and verify the owned page/tab is unchanged. Schema-negative: {"tab_id":"$TAB_ID","request_id":""} must show Schema mismatch before CDP.

After full extension Reload, recapture a new completed GET through 4116 in the new worker/session and repeat; do not reuse the warm request_id. Clean up only the owned attachment/tab after body and errors are recorded.
expected: The actual body from the exact captured public GET decodes to HTML with the independently verified title marker. A nonempty body alone, an old request_id, or an unrelated document is insufficient.
Unknown request_id returns a structured ok:false reason; empty request_id is rejected by local schema. Neither demonstrates permission denial.
A body failure after detach/restart or a changed public page is an environment/fixture limit until a fresh same-session positive control is run; do not infer that the product cannot read bodies.
This direct Tools procedure does not verify the original permissions dimension; a separate proven dispatcher invocation and privileged-card Deny result are still needed for each role.

remaining_unverified: No native browser or role execution occurred. All member/admin result cells and all three original permissions dimensions remain unverified.

The public Selenium pages are outside this repository and may change; each executor must verify exact controls and source marker at run time. The observed 2026-10-07 hashes are provenance, not a permanent byte contract.

read_network_requests currently ignores include_body and clear, drains records regardless of clear, and get_request_body returns a response body; these source limitations must remain explicit in any inventory integration.

Required Chrome debugger permission is install-granted, not an optional Settings toggle. Each role/profile needs a positive permission-status precheck; an unavailable status blocks the positive procedure without proving a handler defect.

Separate dispatcher permission-denial cases are design-needed until the exact agent-call advertisement/invocation and privileged approval card are demonstrated for member and admin. The proposed direct Tools runs must not close any permissions dimension.
